bug_semantics: Ech0 globally ran its i18n middleware before every route and accepted an unauthenticated request's raw Accept-Language value with only TrimSpace. The value reached golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage both directly through ResolveLocale and indirectly through go-i18n's NewLocalizer. x/text's CVE-2022-32149 guard counted '-' but not '_', although its scanner later treats '_' as '-', so a near-1 MiB header composed of malformed underscore-separated tags bypassed the guard and repeatedly exercised the quadratic gobble/memmove path, consuming seconds of CPU per request and enabling denial of service.
flaw_origin: Commit b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516 introduced the entire backend i18n path: internal/i18n/i18n.go added ResolveLocale, the unsanitized goi18n.NewLocalizer wrapper, and Middleware reading Accept-Language, while internal/router/middleware.go installed that middleware globally. Thus the application's exposure originated when attacker-controlled header input was first connected to the vulnerable parser without a size or shape bound; the parser defect itself pre-existed in x/text.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object names author and committer L1nSn0w <l1nsn0w@qq.com>; its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, bot author, or bot committer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/security/advisories/GHSA-mqxv-9rm6-w8qc identifies the unauthenticated global Middleware -> setLocaleContext -> NewLocalizer -> ParseAcceptLanguage path, the '_' bypass and quadratic parser behavior, affected v4.8.2 commit 451c7c10eb1f23f7525c163e83f8b39f46d5aad0, and patched versions 5.0.1+. `git log -L :Middleware:internal/i18n/i18n.go` and `git log -L :NewLocalizer:internal/i18n/i18n.go` trace both vulnerable functions to b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516; that diff creates internal/i18n/i18n.go with `ctx.GetHeader("Accept-Language")`, passes it to ResolveLocale and NewLocalizer, and creates the direct `goi18n.NewLocalizer(bundle, locale, acceptLanguage)` sink. The same commit changes internal/router/middleware.go to call `r.Use(i18nUtil.Middleware())` globally and adds go-i18n/v2 v2.6.1; its resolved x/text dependency is v0.34.0. Direct parent-tree verification with `git ls-tree -r b00c0f7da80cdbf4f4bd84a0c557ae03c88775a6 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go internal/router/middleware.go` returns only internal/router/middleware.go, and `git show b00c0f7da80cdbf4f4bd84a0c557ae03c88775a6:internal/router/middleware.go` has no i18n import or registration. The BIC has one parent and no merge/squash wrapper to decompose. `git rev-parse v4.0.2^{commit}` equals the parent b00c0f7da80cdbf4f4bd84a0c557ae03c88775a6, while `git describe --contains b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516` reports v4.1.0~6, establishing v4.0.2 as immediately pre-introduction and v4.1.0 as the first tagged vulnerable line. Fix a5e77c4af60ead1cad3b3e8e0a3ed6f30892ed09 adds sanitizeAcceptLanguage, caps the combined '-'/'_' separator count at 32, applies it in ResolveLocale and NewLocalizer, and directly closes all sinks. `git describe --contains` reports the fix as v5.0.2~4; v5.0.0 peels to 4deb936608843fab40692788cf299700bb6637bf and retains the vulnerable sinks, v5.0.2 peels to f715214732db93067718150cb3b2bad8fe9be827 and contains the fix, and this full clone has no v5.0.1 tag, so v5.0.2 is the first available tagged release satisfying the advisory's 5.0.1+ patched boundary. Finally, `git cat-file -p b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516` supplies the BIC-only author/committer/message evidence and contains no AI marker.
reasoning: The lifecycle begins immediately after v4.0.2: the single-parent BIC simultaneously created the unsafe parser wrappers, exposed raw request headers to them, and registered the middleware on the global router. The later dc03197eeb4b5f28ebe794f45732cd4d04d53b1c refactor rearranged locale selection and setLocaleContext but retained the same raw Accept-Language-to-NewLocalizer sink, so it is not the introducer. The advisory's inspected v4.8.2 tree and the pre-fix v5.0.0 tag retain the mechanism. The direct fix a5e77c4af60ead1cad3b3e8e0a3ed6f30892ed09 bounds both direct and indirect parser inputs before the first post-fix tag v5.0.2. Parent-tree inspection proves neither internal/i18n/i18n.go nor global i18n registration existed immediately before b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516, and line history proves no later move/refactor is being mistaken for origin. Although the fix commit explicitly has a Claude co-author, protocol requires attribution from the BIC commit object only; the BIC is human-authored/committed with no AI trailer or bot identity. Therefore the causal BIC is closed as NOT_AI.
